Makes a gadget that is meant to show a web page, and returns its handle. The style 1 stops the context menu and 2 stops the user from following links (the link is then given by [HtmlViewEventURL](HtmlViewEventURL)); both are accepted and ignored.

```blitzbasic
Graphics 320, 240, 32, 2
win = CreateWindow("Browser", 10, 10, 300, 200, Desktop(), 3)
html = CreateHtmlView(0, 0, 290, 160, win)
SetGadgetLayout html, 1, 1, 1, 1
HtmlViewGo html, "https://www.blitzbasic.com"
Repeat
Until WaitEvent() = $803
```
@param x       Horizontal position inside the group.
@param y       Vertical position inside the group.
@param width   Width of the gadget.
@param height  Height of the gadget.
@param group   The window or group the gadget is in.
@param style   0 nothing, 1 no context menu, 2 do not follow links. Defaults to 0.
@returns The handle of the gadget.
@gap There is no web browser inside the window yet: the gadget is a frame that shows the address it was sent to, and no page is loaded. Windows could embed WebView for it; Linux and macOS have nothing similar. The original BlitzPlus had this command turned off in its runtime too.
